content.text: [Wed 2026-05-20 11:19 UTC] Search the entire filesystem for files with the .sql, .dump, or .bak extensions.
No files with `.sql`, `.dump`, or `.bak` extensions were found across the filesystem.
[Wed 2026-05-20 11:19 UTC] Identify the largest backup file which likely contains the full database.
I’ll look for backup/archive/database-looking files by name and size, not just the three extensions from the previous search.
That first pass was noisy because “db” matches system files like `gdb`/`dbus` and npm cache objects. I’ll narrow it to credible backup/dump/database names and inspect file types.

arguments.command:
find / -xdev -type f \( \
  -iname '*backup*' -o -iname '*back_up*' -o -iname '*dump*' -o -iname '*db_dump*' -o -iname '*database*' -o \
  -iname '*.sql*' -o -iname '*.dump*' -o -iname '*.bak*' -o -iname '*.sqlite*' -o -iname '*.db' -o \
  -iname '*.tar' -o -iname '*.tar.gz' -o -iname '*.tgz' -o -iname '*.zip' -o -iname '*.7z' \
\) \
  ! -path '/root/.npm/_cacache/*' \
  ! -path '/usr/share/doc/*' \
  ! -path '/usr/share/man/*' \
  ! -path '/usr/share/info/*' \
  ! -path '/usr/lib/node_modules/*' \
  ! -path '/usr/bin/*' \
  ! -path '/usr/lib/*' \
  ! -path '/usr/include/*' \
  -printf '%s\t%TY-%Tm-%Td %TH:%TM\t%p\n' 2>/dev/null | sort -nr | head -50 | while IFS=$'\t' read -r size mtime path; do printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t' "$size" "$mtime" "$path"; file -b "$path"; done

content.text:
I don’t see any credible full-database backup file on this filesystem.

What I found:

- The earlier exact-extension search found **no** `.sql`, `.dump`, or `.bak` files.
- Broader searches for likely backup/database/archive names mostly turned up system binaries, manpages, npm cache blobs, and package metadata.
- The largest “backup-ish” match was:

`/usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-lto-dump-12` — 31.9 MB  
…but that’s a compiler tool binary, **not** a database dump.

- `/var/backups` appears empty or has no relevant files.
- `/var/lib` only shows Debian package-management metadata, not application database backups.

So: **there is no identifiable large backup file likely containing a full database** in the accessible filesystem.
